title: Backlog and release slicing
outcome: Turn product intent into deliverable work: epics and user stories, a clear prioritisation and a release plan the team can commit to.

minimumInputs.help: What should the next releases achieve?
minimumInputs.example: Cut approval time in half and launch to all departments.

minimumInputs.help: Paste or list the work items you have now.
minimumInputs.example: Email approvals, delegation, mobile view, reporting, finance integration.

minimumInputs.help: How much capacity do you have, and what depends on what?
minimumInputs.example: Two developers; finance integration must come before reporting.

minimumInputs.help: Who is the main user of what will be built?
minimumInputs.example: Approving managers who receive invoices for sign-off.

minimumInputs.help: What should the user be able to do that they cannot do today?
minimumInputs.example: Approve an invoice from their phone in under a minute.

minimumInputs.help: What is included in this piece of work, and what is not?
minimumInputs.example: Approval and rejection only; editing invoice details is not included.

minimumInputs.prompt: Acceptance expectations proposed where not confirmed
minimumInputs.help: Optional. How you would know a story is done. Kryterea proposes acceptance criteria where you have none, marked as proposed.
List the items you need to prioritise.
minimumInputs.example: Approval by email, mobile app, supplier portal, reporting dashboard.

minimumInputs.help: What goal should the priorities serve?
minimumInputs.example: Cut approval time in half within six months.

minimumInputs.help: How should items be ranked? Name criteria or a method, or say "suggest one".
minimumInputs.example: Value to the business versus effort; or suggest one.

minimumInputs.help: Nothing to fill in. Effort or value you have not estimated is left blank, never invented.
What goes into the release, and what does it depend on?
minimumInputs.example: Email approvals and delegation; needs the finance connector.

minimumInputs.prompt: Actual release evidence required for delivered notes
minimumInputs.help: Optional. Paste what actually shipped (tickets, change log). Release notes only describe delivered work from real evidence.
What outcome should the roadmap drive?
minimumInputs.example: Every invoice approved within five days.

minimumInputs.help: What initiatives could get you there?
What decides the order, and what depends on what?
minimumInputs.example: Automation saves the most; the portal needs automation first.

minimumInputs.help: Nothing to fill in. Dates you are unsure of are shown as targets, not commitments.
What does the solution cover, and where does it stop?
minimumInputs.example: The approval web app and its email notifications.

minimumInputs.help: Who uses it, what data does it handle, and where or when does it run?
minimumInputs.example: Around 40 managers, invoice and supplier data, used in office hours across two countries.

minimumInputs.help: Which qualities matter most, such as speed, security, availability or accessibility?
minimumInputs.example: Security of supplier bank details, and pages loading in under two seconds.

minimumInputs.help: Nothing to fill in. Any number you have not given (for example a response time) is proposed and marked for confirmation.
What exactly is being estimated?
minimumInputs.example: Building approval routing and the finance connector.

minimumInputs.help: How should it be estimated? Name a method or past work to compare with, or say "suggest one".
minimumInputs.example: Compare with the expense tool we built last year.

minimumInputs.help: What limits apply, and what evidence do you have (past timings, team size)?
minimumInputs.example: Two developers; the expense tool took ten weeks.

minimumInputs.help: Nothing to fill in. Numbers without a basis are left blank, never invented.
